doc_screened_files.reason: Direct panic site in the report: `BorrowSet::build` aborts on "found two uses for 2-phase borrow temporary". The ICE is an invariant failure in the code that records reservation/activation points for two-phase borrows, so this is the strongest root-cause candidate.

This module decides when two-phase borrowing is allowed and whether a two-phase borrow is active from dominator information. That is exactly the machinery closest to the reported temp-use invariant, so it is a likely companion bug or missing special case.

Borrow checking’s conflict decisions come from this file. If the explicit-tail-call path produces an extra use of the receiver temp, the overlap/conflict logic here can be part of why borrow_set sees an unexpected second use.

This file drives the loan-in-scope and kill analyses that borrowck relies on after `BorrowSet` is built. A mis-modeled control-flow edge around `become` or tail-call execution would surface here as a bad loan lifetime/activation pattern.

Method-call confirmation applies the receiver adjustments that create the mutable autoref temporary for `self.cut()`. The reported temp is exactly the kind produced here, so this is a plausible upstream source of the bad two-phase borrow shape.

This is where call expressions are type-checked and receiver adjustments are coordinated. Because the reproducer hinges on a method call under explicit tail-call syntax, this is another likely place where the two-phase borrow temp is introduced incorrectly.

This lowering path handles destination-based expression lowering and control-flow-shaped expressions. The `become self.cut()` surface trigger is likely lowered here, so an explicit-tail-call special case could be creating the extra use that borrow_set later reports.

This is the main MIR type-checking driver that feeds borrowck its region, liveness, and type-test inputs. If the body is being classified in a way that leaves the receiver temp with an unexpected use pattern, the problem can originate here.

This is the top-level entry point for NLL borrow checking. It orchestrates the full path from MIR type checking into region inference and makes the borrow_set failure user-visible, so it is a plausible nearby integration point.

Block lowering controls how temporaries, tail expressions, and branch arms are sequenced in MIR. Because the ICE only appears with a branch containing `become`, block-level lowering is a reasonable place for the temp to gain an extra use path.
